display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Alert: filesystem 99% full on the NGINX LB

div.style: color: rgb(31, 41, 55) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Identify the filesystem from the alert
findmnt --target · df -hT · df -i
never assume /

div.style: color: rgb(31, 41, 55) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Phase 0 — triage, 5 min
systemctl status nginx · bounded curl on the real listener
upstream 5xx rate · dmesg (no nginx -t: it can create files)

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Is NGINX still
serving traffic?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Declare an incident
drain or fail over this LB first,
then diagnose

div.style: color: rgb(31, 41, 55) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
PRESERVE EVIDENCE FIRST (Phase 0b)
access + error log · /etc config · journal
the deleted inode via /proc/pid/fd
stream off-box with pipefail, then verify checksums

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Read-only or erroring
filesystem?
dmesg · mount options

div.style: color: rgb(31, 41, 55) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Storage or filesystem FAULT, not capacity
do NOT remount rw, do NOT fsck while mounted
do NOT delete, compress or truncate: this branch never writes
drain · keep dmesg + device logs · snapshot

div.style: color: rgb(31, 41, 55) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Repair unmounted — rescue media or the volume attached elsewhere —
or replace the instance from an image

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Verify: mount options read-write again, no dmesg errors,
upstream 5xx and latency at baseline

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
df -i
inodes exhausted?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Millions of small files
delete in bounded batches,
then fix what produces them

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Does du disagree
with df?

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
lsof +L1 shows
deleted-but-open files?
key by device+inode

div.style: color: rgb(31, 41, 55) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
#2 CAUSE — deleted log still open
copy the descriptor off-box FIRST
then nginx -s reopen (USR1)

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Hidden under a mount point, or reserved blocks
mount --bind $MOUNT /mnt/fscheck
tune2fs -l | grep reserved

div.style: color: rgb(31, 41, 55) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
du -xh --max-depth=1 on the alerted mount
then drill down
(nice + ionice, bounded)

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Is it
/var/log/nginx?

div.style: color: rgb(31, 41, 55) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
#1 CAUSE — unbounded access/error log
log_format · error_log level · health checks
logrotate state · traffic anomaly as a trigger

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Where is it?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Journal over its cap, often duplicating nginx
journalctl --disk-usage
SystemMaxUse / SystemKeepFree

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
OS logs or a shipper spool
rotation failing silently
logrotate -d /etc/logrotate.conf

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
proxy_temp / client_body_temp
cap proxy_max_temp_file_size
and client_max_body_size

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
proxy_cache_path with no max_size
set max_size + inactive, then reload
never delete cache files by hand

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Core dumps: keep one, cap with MaxUse=
the crash is the real finding

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Package cache, old kernels,
disabled snap revisions

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Ad-hoc dump or capture
move to object storage

div.style: color: rgb(31, 41, 55) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
#3 CAUSE — the filesystem is
smaller than the 64 GB disk
lsblk · vgs · growpart + resize2fs/xfs_growfs

div.style: color: rgb(31, 41, 55) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Phase 3 — recover in this order:
1. evidence verified off-box
2. reopen descriptors
3. grow the filesystem if capacity is unused
4. remove verified disposable data
5. compress/rotate only with headroom
6. truncate last (data is lost)
7. verify df + 5xx + latency, do NOT reload

div.style: color: rgb(31, 41, 55) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Prevent: ship logs off-box · sample · exclude health checks ·
logrotate with postrotate reopen · cap journald, cache, temp, coredumps ·
separate /var/log volume · alert at 80% + predict_linear + inodes + log bytes/s
